properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
properties.digitization_method: NEWLY ADDED 2026-09-16 -- user-flagged that this feature, though already referenced in this dataset's own text (an earlier Block 3 note calls it 'a separate, physically distant open space between Blocks 15 and 7'), was never actually digitized as its own tracked polygon. Figure 6.2.3 labels 'LOUISIANA PASEO' directly as a landscaped pedestrian path running the full north-south length between Block 15 (west) and Blocks 7/11 (east), from Humboldt Street down to 23rd Street, opening into Power Station Park where Block 7 ends. Built here as a 6-vertex polygon using this project's own already-committed, GDAL/TPS-corrected corners for Block 15's east edge and Block 7/Block 11's west edges directly (not independently re-measured), so it shares an exact boundary with all three blocks by construction -- zero gap, zero overlap -- and its south end sits flush with Power Station Park's own west edge (also built from Block 11's same NW corner), so the two connect exactly as the diagram shows.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a simplified straight-sided approximation of a landscaped pedestrian paseo; the diagram does not show this as a simple rectangle (it likely has planting/path detail not captured here). Positional accuracy matches whatever the adjoining Block 15/7/11 files currently carry (see their own accuracy_caveat) since this polygon is built directly from their vertices.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site.
properties.regulatory_context: A landscaped pedestrian paseo per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label, connecting Humboldt Street to 23rd Street and opening into Power Station Park.
properties.notes: Newly added 2026-09-16; previously mentioned only in passing in other blocks' notes, never tracked as its own feature.
